title: Best GPU for i5-14600K (2026): 5 Cards for Gaming and Editing
description: The RX 9070 XT is the best GPU for an i5-14600K: 16 GB and RTX 5070 Ti-class raster for $600–$730, an even 1440p match. 5 picks, plus 4K editing advice.
dek: A 14-core Raptor Lake Refresh chip keeps upper-mid-range cards busy. These five picks cover 1080p to 4K, video editing, and the BIOS update this CPU needs first.
intro: The Radeon RX 9070 XT is the best GPU for a Core i5-14600K in 2026. For $600–$730 it matches an RTX 5070 Ti in raster games, carries 16 GB, and at 1440p the 14600K and the card are evenly matched, so neither one waits on the other.

This page is for owners of Intel's 14-core i5, and of the near-identical i5-13600K. It answers which card pairs best for gaming, which suits 4K video editing, and how far up the range the CPU can go before it becomes the limit. It also covers the microcode BIOS update every 13th and 14th generation owner should install.
quickAnswer: Buy the RX 9070 XT ($600–$730) for 1440p gaming. For video editing or ray tracing, the RTX 5070 Ti ($750–$900) is the better pair. The RTX 5080 ($1,000–$1,300) is the 4K ceiling. The RTX 5070 ($550–$650) is the value choice, and the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB ($430–$480) suits 1080p. Install the latest BIOS before anything else.

picks.label: Best Overall Match
picks.skipIf: you edit video in Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve, or play path-traced games
writeup: The Core i5-14600K games roughly like a Ryzen 5 9600X, per our [Intel vs AMD CPU equivalents chart](/intel-vs-amd-cpu-equivalents/). It has six performance cores and eight efficient cores, and that is enough to keep a fast 1440p card busy in most games.

The RX 9070 XT is the card that uses that headroom best for the money. Independent reviews put it close to an RTX 5070 Ti in raster games, which usually costs more, and it has the same 16 GB of memory. FSR 4, AMD's machine-learning upscaler, is a large step over older FSR versions, though fewer games support it than DLSS.

At 1440p, most games are limited by the card rather than the 14600K, so the pairing is balanced. At 1080p in fast esports titles, the CPU can become the limit, but at frame rates beyond what most monitors show.
AMD rates it at 304 W and partner cards often run higher. The 14600K can draw well over 150 W under full load, so an 850 W supply is the comfortable size for the pair.
cons: Ray tracing a tier behind NVIDIA
Weaker app support for video editing than NVIDIA

picks.label: Best for Video Editing
picks.bestFor: 4K video editing, streaming and ray-traced games
picks.skipIf: you only play raster games and want the lowest price for the speed
writeup: If you edit 4K video as well as game, the RTX 5070 Ti is the better pair. Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve make broad use of NVIDIA's CUDA and NVENC hardware, and NVIDIA lists hardware decoding of 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC on RTX 50 series cards, a format many mirrorless cameras record.

Its 16 GB of memory gives room for 4K timelines with effects and color grading. In games it matches the RX 9070 XT in raster and pulls ahead with ray tracing on, with DLSS 4 and multi frame generation on top.
NVIDIA recommends a 750 W supply; with a 14600K, 850 W leaves comfortable headroom. Most models use a 12V-2x6 connector.
pros: Strong in Premiere Pro and Resolve
cons: Usually costs more than the RX 9070 XT

picks.label: Best for 4K
picks.bestFor: 4K gaming where the graphics card does nearly all the work
picks.skipIf: you play at 1080p or 1440p, where the 14600K limits it in CPU-heavy games
writeup: The RTX 5080 is the highest card that makes sense with a 14600K, and mainly at 4K. At that resolution the graphics card sets the frame rate in almost every game, so a 14-core i5 gives up little compared with a more expensive chip.

At 1440p, the 14600K starts to cap frame rates in CPU-heavy games before the RTX 5080 is fully used. Our [RX 9070 XT vs RTX 5080 comparison](/compare/rx-9070-xt-vs-rtx-5080/) shows how much the step up buys when the card is the limit.
For editing, it adds speed in GPU-heavy effects and exports. NVIDIA recommends an 850 W supply for its 360 W rating.
pros: Top 4K performance short of the RTX 5090

picks.label: Best Value Pick
picks.bestFor: 1440p at high settings for less money
picks.skipIf: you keep cards five years or more; 12 GB is its limit
writeup: The RTX 5070 is the lower-cost way to a capable 1440p system on a 14600K. It handles high settings at that resolution in most games, and DLSS 4 with multi frame generation stretches it further where supported.

Its 12 GB is enough for 1440p gaming today and for 1080p and light 4K editing, but heavier 4K timelines are more comfortable on a 16 GB card. Our [RTX 5070 vs RTX 5070 Ti comparison](/compare/rtx-5070-vs-rtx-5070-ti/) shows what the extra money buys.
At 250 W it is easy to power. NVIDIA recommends 650 W; with a 14600K, 750 W is the safer choice.
cons: RX 9070 is faster in raster at a similar price

picks.label: Best for 1080p
picks.skipIf: you play at 1440p with high settings; an RTX 5070 or RX 9070 XT suits the CPU better
writeup: Not every 14600K build needs a big card. For 1080p, the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB gives high settings and 16 GB of memory for $430–$480, and the 14600K will rarely hold it back.

Its PCIe 5.0 x8 link runs at full speed on Z790 boards that wire the slot for PCIe 5.0, and current x8 cards lose little on PCIe 4.0. The 16 GB also helps in light 4K editing, where the 8 GB version runs short.
At 180 W it runs on a 650 W supply with a 14600K. It is a sensible holding card: this CPU can drive something much faster later.

ranking.intro: These picks combine manufacturer specifications, published CPU-scaling reviews of Raptor Lake processors, and owner reports from LGA 1700 builds. None of these pairings were bench-tested by Enthusiast Review; statements about where the 14600K limits a card reflect what independent reviewers have widely reported.
criteria: The 14600K keeps cards up to RTX 5070 Ti level busy at 1440p, so each pick is matched to the resolution where it is fully used.
Raster performance per dollar counted heavily for gaming, since most games still rely on it.
For video work, CUDA, NVENC and hardware decode support in Premiere Pro and Resolve counted.
Cards with 16 GB ranked above 12 GB alternatives at similar speed, for games and 4K timelines.
The 14600K can draw well over 150 W, so we sized supplies for the full system.
ranking.why: The RX 9070 XT won because it gives RTX 5070 Ti-class raster speed and 16 GB for less, and it balances the 14600K at 1440p.

mentions.text: The RX 9070 is an efficient 1440p card with 16 GB that runs on a 650 W supply. It is a good choice if you want to keep an existing smaller supply, but the RX 9070 XT costs little more and suits the 14600K's speed better.
An RTX 5090 is wasted on a 14600K except at 4K with maximum settings, or for its 32 GB in heavy creative work. Below 4K the CPU limits it, and the 575 W rating calls for a 1,000 W supply.

Upgrading to a Core i9-14900K on the same board adds cores for exports and rendering, but only a small gain in games and a large rise in power. For gaming, the money is better spent on the graphics card.

sections.h: Update the BIOS First: Does the 14600K Need the Microcode Fix?
body: Yes. In 2024, Intel attributed instability reports on 13th and 14th generation desktop processors to elevated operating voltage and released microcode updates through motherboard BIOS updates. The i5-14600K and i5-13600K are among the chips covered. Intel also extended the warranty on affected boxed processors, per its announcements; check the current terms.
Install the latest BIOS for your exact board, then load the default or Intel-recommended power profile. Do it before installing the new card, so any crashes afterward are easier to trace.
list: Download the newest BIOS for your board model from the maker's support page.
Update with the current graphics card still installed.
Load Intel default power settings after updating.
Then install the new card and the latest GPU driver.

sections.h: Which GPU Pairs Best With an i5-14600K?
body: At 1440p, the RX 9070 XT or RTX 5070 Ti. Both are fast enough that the 14600K and the card share the work evenly, and both have 16 GB. At 1080p, an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB or RX 9070 is enough, because beyond that the CPU sets the frame rate in many games. At 4K, the RTX 5080 is the ceiling worth paying for.
Some searches call this chip the i7-14600K; it is a Core i5. The i7 in this generation is the 20-core [i7-14700K](/best-gpu-for-core-i7-14700k/), which can feed a slightly faster card.

sections.h: Which GPU Pairs With an i5-13600K to Minimize Bottleneck in 4K Video Editing?
body: An RTX 5070 Ti, or an RTX 5080 for heavy effects work. The i5-13600K has the same 14-core layout as the 14600K with slightly lower clocks, so the same cards suit it. In 4K editing, the bottleneck is usually decoding the camera footage and the timeline's effects, not raw CPU speed.

That is where NVIDIA's hardware helps: NVDEC and NVENC handle decoding and exporting, and CUDA speeds up effects in Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve. On the K models (not KF), Intel's integrated UHD Graphics 770 adds Quick Sync, which many editing apps use to decode H.264 and HEVC footage. Use 16 GB of video memory or more for 4K timelines with grading and noise reduction, and 32 GB of system RAM or more.

sections.h: Will an i5-14600K Bottleneck an RTX 5080?
body: At 4K, rarely. At 1440p and 1080p, in CPU-heavy games such as large strategy and simulation titles, the 14600K does limit an RTX 5080. If you play below 4K, an RTX 5070 Ti or RX 9070 XT is the better match.

Our [bottleneck calculator](/tools/bottleneck-calculator/) shows the balance for any pairing and resolution. For an older card, the [old GeForce equivalents chart](/old-nvidia-gpu-equivalents/) shows how much faster each new card is.

sections.h: Does the i5-14600K Support PCIe 5.0 Graphics Cards?
body: The CPU does, but the slot speed depends on the board. Many Z790 boards and some Z690 models wire the main slot for PCIe 5.0, while B760 boards typically run it at PCIe 4.0. Every card on this page runs at full speed on PCIe 4.0 x16.
Resizable BAR is supported on LGA 1700; enable it with Above 4G Decoding in the BIOS. The 14600K works with DDR4 or DDR5 depending on the board, and either is fine for gaming.

sections.h: What Power Supply Do You Need?
body: Size it for the whole system. Intel rates the 14600K at 125 W base and 181 W maximum turbo power, which is far more than older i5 chips under an all-core load like a video export.

As a guide with a 14600K: 650 W for an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, 750 W for an RTX 5070, 850 W for an RX 9070 XT or RTX 5070 Ti, and 850–1,000 W for an RTX 5080. Our [PSU calculator](/tools/psu-calculator/) adds up a full build, and our [best PSU for RX 9070 XT](/best-psu-for-rx-9070-xt/) guide lists units that fit.

sections.h: Should You Upgrade the CPU Instead?
body: Not for gaming. The 14600K keeps cards up to an RTX 5070 Ti busy at 1440p, and LGA 1700 has no newer generation to move to, so the graphics card is the better place for the money.

If you edit or render heavily, a Core i7-14700K or i9-14900K on the same board adds cores for exports, at a large cost in power. For a new build focused on gaming, a Ryzen 7 9800X3D is faster in games.

mistakes: Intel's fix for 13th and 14th generation instability reports arrives through BIOS updates. Install it before changing the graphics card, so a crash afterward is not blamed on the new part.
Choosing a gaming card for an editing workload
If you edit 4K video, the decode and effects support in your editing app matters as much as frame rates. Check that your app accelerates the card's hardware before buying.
Buying an 8 GB card for 4K timelines
8 GB cards run short in 4K editing with grading and effects, and already limit textures in some games. Choose 16 GB on a 14600K build.
Pairing an RTX 5090 with a 14-core i5 for 1440p
At 1440p the 14600K limits an RTX 5090 in many games. An RTX 5080 gives most of the result for about half the price.
Using a KF chip and expecting Quick Sync
The 14600KF has no integrated graphics, so editing apps cannot use Intel's Quick Sync decoder. Rely on the graphics card's decoder instead.
bottomLine: For an i5-14600K, the RX 9070 XT is the card to buy in 2026 for gaming: RTX 5070 Ti-class raster, 16 GB, and an even match at 1440p. For 4K video editing on a 14600K or 13600K, choose the RTX 5070 Ti. The RTX 5080 is the 4K ceiling, the RTX 5070 the value pick, and the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB the 1080p pick. Update the BIOS for Intel's microcode fix first.

faqs.q: What is the best GPU for an i5-14600K?
faqs.a: The RX 9070 XT for 1440p gaming. It matches an RTX 5070 Ti in raster games for less and has 16 GB. The RTX 5070 Ti is the better pick for video editing and ray tracing, and the RTX 5080 for 4K.

faqs.q: What is the ideal GPU for an i5-14600K?
faqs.a: One that matches your resolution: an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB at 1080p, an RX 9070 XT or RTX 5070 Ti at 1440p, and an RTX 5080 at 4K. Faster cards than those are often limited by the CPU.
No. The 14600K is a Core i5 with 14 cores and 20 threads. The i7 in Intel's 14th generation is the i7-14700K, with 20 cores and 28 threads.

faqs.q: What GPU pairs with an i5-13600K for 4K video editing?
faqs.a: An RTX 5070 Ti, or an RTX 5080 for heavy effects. NVIDIA's decoders, encoders and CUDA support speed up Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve, and 16 GB of video memory suits 4K timelines.

faqs.q: Will an i5-14600K bottleneck an RTX 5070 Ti?
faqs.a: Rarely at 1440p or 4K. At 1080p in CPU-heavy or esports games it can, but at frame rates above what most monitors show.

faqs.q: What PSU do I need for an i5-14600K and RX 9070 XT?
faqs.a: A quality 850 W supply. The RX 9070 XT is rated at 304 W and partner cards often run higher, while the 14600K is rated at up to 181 W at maximum turbo.

faqs.q: Do I need a BIOS update for the i5-14600K?
faqs.a: Yes. Intel released microcode updates through motherboard BIOS updates to address instability reports on 13th and 14th generation desktop chips, including the 14600K. Install the latest BIOS before other upgrades.
